name: Montana Domino Rummy
description: Montana Domino Rummy is a western domino rummy-style game typically played with multiple double-six sets to provide sufficient tile supply. This entry models the shared tile family and supply using four double-six sets; the rummy-style sequencing and layout objectives are expressed as a table profile layered on top of the tile set.

history.origins: Montana-style domino rummy formats are encountered as modern table games that use dominoes in structured layouts resembling rummy sequencing goals.
timeline: Modern era: circulated through social play and rules collections.
history.cultural: Played as a casual social game where the table agrees on the exact layout and scoring profile.
history.evolution: Using multiple sets increases supply and duplication, supporting larger layouts and longer sessions.

setup.deck: Four double-6 domino sets combined and mixed.
setup.dealing: Tiles are distributed according to the chosen layout profile; any remaining tiles may be held aside or used as a draw pool by table rules.
setup.equipment: Domino sets and an agreed layout/scoring profile.

rules.objective: Complete the target rummy-style layout under the agreed profile using legal placements and reach the match end condition with the best score.
rules.gameplay: Players place tiles according to a structured layout profile that defines placement constraints and progression goals. The underlying tile identity remains the standard western double-six family; the profile defines whether draws are allowed, how blocking is resolved, and how completion is scored.
keyRules: Tile identity is standard western double-six; multiple sets introduce duplication.
Placement legality and layout progression are profile-defined for the Montana rummy format.
Hand-end and scoring depend on the match profile in use.

strategy.basic: Focus on moves that increase future placement options in the layout.
strategy.intermediate: Because duplicates exist, plan for multiple competing placement routes rather than relying on a single missing tile.
strategy.advanced: Optimize layout flexibility to avoid dead ends, while denying opponents key placement opportunities when interaction exists.
tips: Prefer moves that open multiple next placements.
Avoid consuming a flexible tile too early if the profile allows alternative placements later.

synthesis.shortDescription: Montana Domino Rummy is a layout-based domino rummy format using four double-six sets to supply large, duplicated tile pools.
